correctness.rationale: For any existing affine plane of order q>=2, point-line incidence axioms yield BB^T=qI+J and B^TB=(q-1)I+J-H. The zero-sum powered-distance form decomposes into parallel-class contrasts of dimension q with eigenvalue 2^p((q-1)2^p-q), q^2-1 paired 2x2 blocks with diagonal -2^p,-4^p and coupling sqrt(q)(1-3^p), and one global point-versus-line contrast. The paired determinants stay positive up to alpha_q=log_2(q/(q-1)); the scalar sector stays negative by the stated 3^p concavity bound; the parallel eigenvalue changes sign exactly at alpha_q. This proves CND iff p<=alpha_q and strictness below, with endpoint nullities q for q>=3 and 5 for q=2. Schoenberg and centered Gram rank yield PSD for every t and Euclidean dimensions. q2, p=0, non-Desarguesian applicability and nonexistence of some q are explicitly bounded. Finite numerical spectra cannot replace these sector inequalities.

value.rationale: A full negative-type exponent and critical Euclidean embedding-dimension classification for Levi graphs of any affine plane is a motivated metric-geometry invariant. The parallel-class nullity and exceptional q=2 effect are nontrivial structural information beyond general Schoenberg equivalence.

limitations: Claims require an existing finite affine plane, not that every positive integer q admits one.
The theorem describes positivity for all t>0, not one fixed Gaussian scale; theoretical extension to arbitrary resolvable designs was not proved.
